controlHint.createProject: Open a form for adding a new project to the current working copy.
controlHint.createTask: Open a form for adding a new task to the selected project.
controlHint.createMilestone: Open a form for adding a new milestone to the selected project.
controlHint.openProjectArchive: Open this project's archive view. The counters show archived milestones and archived tasks currently available there; opening it does not restore, delete, or otherwise change them.
controlHint.backToProjectPlan: Return to the project's current plan and close archive mode. Archived data is not restored or deleted; only the view and URL change.
controlHint.outsideActiveMilestones: Show only active tasks that do not belong to an active milestone: tasks with no milestone, a missing milestone reference, or an archived milestone. Press again to clear this quick filter; task data is not changed.
controlHint.summaryTotal: Show all tasks in the current milestone and advanced-filter scope. This clears the summary quick filter and the separate status filter while preserving the milestone and advanced conditions.
controlHint.summaryActive: Show tasks with the dedicated in-progress status. Other active states, such as review or blocked, are not included. Press again to clear this quick filter.
controlHint.summaryBlocked: Show tasks with the dedicated blocked status. Press again to clear the filter; no task status is changed.
controlHint.summaryOverdue: Show incomplete tasks whose effective finish in the primary schedule is before today. A parent task's finish may be derived from its subtasks.
controlHint.summaryCompleted: Show tasks whose status belongs to the Done semantic category. This filters the list without changing any status.
controlHint.openMilestoneDetails: Open this milestone's details in the side panel while preserving the current filters and archive mode in the URL. The milestone and its tasks are not changed.
controlHint.openTaskDetails: Open this task in the side panel while preserving the current filters, milestone, and archive mode in the URL. The task's status and order are not changed.
controlHint.openPerson: Open this person's profile with assignments, workload, calendar, and availability. Navigation does not change data.
controlHint.openProject: Open this project's plan with milestones, tasks, dates, and effort. Navigation does not change or publish data.
controlHint.openMilestone: Open this milestone inside its project. Navigation does not move tasks or change the milestone.
controlHint.createSubtask: Open a form for a task under the current task. The new task uses the same project and milestone, and the current assignees are copied as an editable initial selection.
controlHint.openMoveTask: Open the move editor for this task and its entire subtree. Nothing changes until a target project, milestone, optional parent, and the final move action are confirmed.
controlHint.moveTask: Atomically move the task and its full subtree to the selected scope. Comments and time entries move with it, and internal subtask links are preserved. Validation rejects the whole operation for a cycle, mismatched milestone, or cross-project dependency.
controlHint.addTimeEntry: Create a new active time entry for this task. It immediately contributes to total hours, first and last activity, the actual track, and reports without changing the task's planned estimate.
controlHint.scheduleTrackTab: Switch the schedule variant being edited. Each track stores its dates, planned effort, and dependencies independently; changing tabs does not copy or recalculate values. The primary marker identifies the project's default working track.
controlHint.addAssignee: Open the people picker and add another assignee to this task.
controlHint.generateDraftId: Generate a valid, unique ID for the new working copy.
controlHint.createDraft: Create an isolated Git branch and worktree for a new set of changes.
controlHint.switchToUi: Give editing control back to GitPM forms after external changes are synchronized.
controlHint.switchToExternal: Give an external tool editing control; GitPM forms become read-only.
controlHint.closeDraft: Prevent further edits while keeping this working copy available to reopen.

controlHint.cleanupDraft: Remove this working copy's worktree and branch after confirmation.

admin.calendarNotFound: Calendar {id} was not found. It may have been deleted.
admin.configurationBlocked: This change is blocked by existing repository data. Update the listed documents first.

admin.presetStandardDescription: Monday to Friday, without public holidays. This is a neutral custom calendar, not a production calendar.
admin.presetRussia2026Description: Official 2026 production calendar for a five-day workweek. Later Russian years are not included until the Government approves them.
admin.presetUnitedStatesFederalDescripti: OPM federal holiday schedule for Monday-to-Friday employees, including Friday/Monday observance. State, local and company holidays may differ.
admin.presetEveryDayDescription: All seven weekdays are working. Useful for continuous operations and on-call schedules.
admin.applyPresetHint: Replaces working weekdays and non-working dates in this form. Nothing changes until you save.
admin.slugHint: Technical slugs identify configuration values. Add or remove values here; referenced values can only be deactivated or must be unlinked first.
admin.calendarsDescription: Working calendars define working weekdays and holidays for people, workload calculations, and project schedules. The default calendar is assigned to new people.
admin.settingsTasksDescription: These shared values define how tasks are classified and move through their lifecycle in every project.
admin.statusesDescription: Lifecycle stages used by task lists, boards, filters, and completion calculations.
admin.issueTypesDescription: Shared labels for classifying the kind of work represented by a task.
admin.settingsPlanningDescription: Configure schedule variants such as a baseline, current plan, and actual work, plus the defaults projects receive.
admin.scheduleTracksDescription: Defines which plan and actual-work variants projects can use and the roles assigned to them by default.
admin.settingsTimeTrackingDescription: Configure the shared categories available when people record time.
admin.workCategoriesDescription: Labels used to classify time entries and summarize effort in reports.
admin.scheduleTracksHint: Keep contract or baseline dates, current expectations, and work already performed as separate views of the same schedule.
admin.scheduleTracksDefinitionsHint: Give each variant a recognizable name, choose how its data appears, and—for variants filled in by users—select what they can enter.
admin.defaultProjectPlanningHint: Choose which variants projects receive and what each one is used for. Individual projects can override these defaults.
admin.scheduleTracksKindsHint: Variants filled in by users store the selected planning data. The actual-work variant is calculated from active time entries and cannot be edited as a plan.
admin.scheduleTracksUsageHint: Define the variants first, then choose which projects receive by default and assign the main, workload, comparison, and display roles. Individual projects can override these settings.
admin.trackDisplayNameHint: This name appears in tasks, the Gantt chart, dashboards, and reports.
admin.manualTrackChoiceHint: Dates, planned effort, and dependencies are edited in projects and tasks.
admin.actualTrackChoiceHint: GitPM builds it automatically from active time entries; users cannot edit it as a plan.
admin.singleActualTrackHint: The repository already has an actual-work variant. Only one can be calculated from time tracking.
admin.trackDataFieldsHint: A manual variant needs at least one type of data.
admin.capabilityDependenciesDescription: Tasks that must be completed first
admin.actualTrackCalculationHint: Start is the first work date, finish is the last work date, and effort is the sum of recorded hours. Voided entries are excluded.
admin.manualTrackUsageDatesEffort: Can be used as the main schedule, for workload calculations, and as a comparison plan.
admin.manualTrackUsageDates: Can be used as the main schedule or a comparison plan. Add planned effort to use it for workload calculations.
admin.manualTrackUsageNoDates: This is an additional data variant. Add dates before using it as the main schedule or a comparison plan.
admin.actualTrackUsage: Enable it for a project to show actual activity in the Gantt chart, dashboards, and reports.
admin.trackTechnicalIdHint: Stable internal ID referenced by project and task data. It cannot be renamed here.
admin.addTrackHint: New variants start as manual and allow dates. You can change the name and available data after adding one.
admin.newTrackTechnicalIdHint: Use lowercase Latin letters, digits, and internal hyphens, for example baseline or contract-plan.

planning.heading: Project planning
planning.advancedProjectSettingsHint: Change tracks and their roles only when this project should differ from the repository defaults.
planning.introduction: A track is an independent version of the schedule for the same project, milestones, and tasks. Use several tracks when you need to keep the current plan, a committed or baseline plan, and actual activity separate. If one working plan is enough, you do not need to enable every track.
planning.customNamesHint: Names such as Commitment or Working plan are configured by your repository administrator. A name is only a label: the Manual or Actual marker and the available data below explain how the track behaves.
planning.enabledTracksHint: Enable only the schedule versions this project uses. Disabling a track hides it from project planning without deleting the track definition for the rest of the repository. A track with saved schedule data must be cleared before it can be disabled.
planning.primaryTrackHint: The project's active working schedule. Its dates are used wherever GitPM needs one main project timeline, including the plan summary and the primary layer of the Gantt chart.
planning.workloadTrackHint: The source of planned dates and effort hours for team capacity and workload calculations. Only a manual track that stores both dates and effort can be selected.
planning.comparisonTrackHint: An optional reference schedule used to show variance from the primary plan, for example a baseline or committed dates. Select None if this project does not need plan-versus-baseline comparison.
planning.dashboardTracksHint: Choose the additional tracks that should be selected initially in multi-track views such as the Gantt chart. This affects display defaults only; it does not change the primary schedule or workload calculations.
planning.rolesHint: Assign one enabled track to each calculation role. The same manual track can be both primary and workload when it contains dates and effort.
planning.manualTrackHint: Manual track. Project dates, planned effort, and dependencies are entered by users according to its enabled data: {capabilities}.
planning.actualTrackHint: Actual track. GitPM calculates it automatically from time entries; it is not edited as a plan.
planning.trackInUse: This project already has schedule data in the track. Clear that data before disabling it.
planning.trackRequired: This track is currently the only valid choice for a required role. Enable a suitable alternative first.

repositoryConnection.heading: Repository connection
repositoryConnection.description: GitPM commits in the selected checkout and publishes its active branch directly to origin.
repositoryConnection.managedExternally: This connection is controlled by environment variables and is read-only here.
repositoryConnection.originHelp: GitPM publishes the active branch here and pulls updates. Do not embed HTTP(S) user information, passwords, or tokens. An SSH user such as git@ is allowed. Examples: http://gitlab.local/group/project.git, https://gitlab.example/group/project.git, git@gitlab.example:group/project.git.
repositoryConnection.gitlabSectionHelp: Required for OAuth login, member role checks, and Merge Requests. Without it GitPM can still publish over SSH or an HTTP(S) token, but Merge Requests are unavailable.
repositoryConnection.gitlabUrlHelp: Your GitLab address without the project path. Used for login and the GitLab API, not for git operations.
repositoryConnection.gitlabProjectHelp: A group/project path. It must match the path in the origin URL. Used for membership checks and Merge Requests.
repositoryConnection.clientIdHelp: The public OAuth Application ID of the GitPM app in GitLab (not a secret). If one GitLab field is set, all three are required and the origin URL must point to the same project on the same instance.
repositoryConnection.credentialNote: Do not enter passwords or tokens here. After saving, click "Sign in to GitLab": GitPM opens the GitLab authorization page, receives a short-lived token, and keeps it only in server memory — never in config, logs, or the URL. After a server restart you must sign in again. Plain HTTP sends credentials and repository data without encryption; use it only on a trusted local network.
repositoryConnection.sshNote: For SSH, access is provided by an administrator-provisioned key (GITPM_SSH_KEY_PATH or an ssh-agent). GitPM never stores, reads, or logs the key and never writes it to config. Use a passwordless URL above.
repositoryConnection.httpsTokenNote: For HTTP(S) without GitLab, access is provided by an administrator token (the GITPM_REMOTE_TOKEN environment variable). The token lives only in process memory and is never entered in this form. Plain HTTP sends it without transport encryption.
repositoryConnection.mrNote: Merge Requests are supported only for GitLab. Publishing over SSH or an HTTP(S) token pushes the branch to origin, but MR through GitPM is unavailable.
repositoryConnection.buttonsDisabledHint: "Sign in to GitLab" and "Test connection" become available once the GitLab block is filled in or an origin is configured, respectively.
repositoryConnection.securityHint: Do not embed HTTP(S) usernames, passwords, or tokens in the URL; an SSH username such as git@ is part of a normal SSH address. Credentials stay only in server memory and are never written to Git configuration. Use plain HTTP only on a trusted local network.
repositoryConnection.changeConfirm: Change the publication origin to {url}? Existing local commits and files will not be changed.
repositoryConnection.error.GIT_URL_INVAL: The repository URL is invalid: use an HTTP(S) or SSH URL with no embedded username, password, or token.
repositoryConnection.error.GITLAB_URL_IN: The GitLab instance URL is invalid: provide the HTTP or HTTPS instance origin only, without the project path.
repositoryConnection.error.GITLAB_PROJEC: The GitLab project is invalid: provide a group/project path.
repositoryConnection.error.GITLAB_CLIENT: The OAuth Application ID is invalid.
repositoryConnection.error.GITLAB_CONFIG: When configuring GitLab, all three fields are required: instance URL, project, and OAuth Application ID.
repositoryConnection.error.GIT_REMOTE_RE: Set the origin URL first, then the GitLab parameters.
repositoryConnection.error.GIT_REMOTE_PR: The origin URL and the GitLab project must identify the same project on the same GitLab instance.
repositoryConnection.error.REPOSITORY_CO: Confirm the origin change by repeating the request with the same confirmation value.
The connection is controlled by environment variables and cannot be changed from this form.
repositoryConnection.error.GITLAB_NOT_CO: GitLab is not configured. Sign in after filling in the GitLab integration block.
repositoryConnection.error.SESSION_INVAL: The session is missing or expired. Sign in to GitLab again.
repositoryConnection.credentialNoteIdent: GitLab OAuth is used only for your identity and requests read_user. Fetch, push, role checks, and Merge Requests use the administrator-provisioned Project Access Token, which is never sent to the browser or stored in your session. Your GitLab Public email is required to create a commit.

advancedView.field.title: Title

fieldHint.locale: Changes the interface language only. Stored portfolio data, identifiers, Git commits, and locale-neutral CLI JSON are not translated or rewritten.
fieldHint.currentDraft: Selects the working copy shown by the interface. Each draft has its own branch, fingerprint, writer mode, and uncommitted changes; switching does not merge or publish anything.
fieldHint.draftId: Unique ID for a new isolated working copy and part of its Git branch name. Use 1–128 ASCII letters, digits, and hyphens, starting with a letter or digit. It cannot be renamed after creation.
fieldHint.name: The human-readable name shown in lists, links, reports, and exports. It may be changed later without changing the entity's immutable technical ID or canonical file path.
fieldHint.title: A concise task heading shown in the task tree, board, search, reports, and history. Put the detailed context and acceptance information in Description instead.
fieldHint.description: Optional Markdown-capable explanatory text stored with the entity. Use it for scope, context, constraints, or acceptance details; it does not change scheduling or validation by itself.
fieldHint.status: Selects a configured status. Its status category—backlog, active, done, or cancelled—drives completion grouping and progress calculations; changing status does not automatically record time.
fieldHint.type: Classifies a task using the repository's task-type directory. Types are labels for filtering and reporting; they do not independently change dates, effort, or workflow rules.
fieldHint.owner: The person accountable for the project. This is distinct from task assignees and does not automatically assign that person to every task.
fieldHint.project: Limits the current view or operation to one project. Project scope is strict: selecting a project does not include entities from other projects.
fieldHint.targetProject: The project that will own the moved task and its subtree. The task keeps its immutable ID, while its canonical path and project reference are updated together.
fieldHint.projectGroup: An optional directory grouping for projects. It affects organization and filtering, not project ownership, permissions, schedules, or entity IDs.
fieldHint.newProjectGroup: Creates and immediately assigns a new group name. Leading or trailing whitespace is removed and a name equal to an existing group is rejected.
fieldHint.milestone: The project milestone that contains or filters the task. A subtask inherits its parent's milestone, so moving a hierarchy cannot silently split it across milestones.
fieldHint.parent: Optional task directly above this one in the project hierarchy. Choose a task to make the current task its subtask, or choose No parent task to keep it at the top level. A task cannot be its own parent or a descendant's parent; parent and child must stay in the same project and milestone. Selecting a parent also adopts that parent's milestone.
fieldHint.targetParent: Optional task in the selected target project and milestone that will become the parent of the moved subtree root. No parent keeps the moved task as a root. Existing links inside its subtree are preserved, and the moved task or any of its descendants cannot be selected.
fieldHint.targetMilestone: The milestone in the target project that will be assigned to the moved task and every descendant. No milestone moves the entire subtree outside active milestones. The parent picker is then limited to tasks in that same target milestone, or to tasks with no milestone.
fieldHint.assignees: People expected to work on the task. Assignees feed responsibility views and workload allocation; selecting several people does not duplicate the task's total estimate for each person.
fieldHint.assigneeSearch: Searches active people by name or email before adding them as assignees. It only narrows this picker and does not change the people directory.
fieldHint.lifecycle: Chooses whether lists show active, archived, or all entities. Archive preserves history and references; it is different from permanent deletion.
fieldHint.scheduleStart: The first calendar date of this schedule window. It belongs to the selected manual schedule track and must not be later than Finish when both are set.
fieldHint.scheduleFinish: The last calendar date of the schedule window or the milestone due date. It is inclusive and must not precede Start when the same window has both dates.
fieldHint.estimate: Planned effort in person-hours for the selected manual track, not elapsed duration. Enter a non-negative value in quarter-hour increments; actual time is recorded separately.
fieldHint.dependencies: Tasks that must precede this task in the selected schedule track. Dependencies are project-scoped, cannot point to the task itself or its descendants, and are used for schedule diagnostics and Gantt links.
fieldHint.projectTracks: Controls which repository schedule tracks this project uses and how they are interpreted. Disabling an in-use or required track is blocked to avoid hiding stored schedule data.
fieldHint.enabledTracks: Schedule variants available to this project. Each track keeps independent values; a track cannot be disabled while project, milestone, or task data still uses it.
fieldHint.dashboardTracks: Enabled tracks shown together in overview displays. These checkboxes control visibility only: hiding a track does not delete its dates, effort, or dependencies.
fieldHint.primaryTrack: The manual date track treated as the project's main working schedule in plan views and default task editing. It must be enabled and support dates.
fieldHint.workloadTrack: The enabled manual track used to calculate team allocation. It must support both dates and effort because planned hours are spread across the task window and assignees' availability.
fieldHint.comparisonTrack: An optional enabled date track used as the baseline for variance comparisons. Choosing None removes comparison indicators but does not delete schedule values from any track.
fieldHint.timePerson: The person whose work is being recorded, which need not be the current GitPM user. New entries allow active people; a correction may retain an archived historical person.
fieldHint.timeDate: The calendar date on which the work was actually performed. Active entries use these dates to calculate First activity, Last activity, actual windows, and period reports.
fieldHint.timeHours: Actual person-hours spent on this task on the selected date. Enter a positive number in 0.25-hour increments; these hours are summed independently of the planned estimate.
fieldHint.timeCategory: The configured kind of work, such as regular work, support, or warranty. Categories make actual-effort reports filterable; only active categories can be used for new entries.
fieldHint.timeNote: Optional short context for the time entry, for example what was done or why the work belongs to this category. It is stored with the immutable actual-work record.
fieldHint.actualHeading: Actual effort records work already performed on this task. Each row is an auditable person-and-date record; active rows build the actual schedule track and reports without changing the planned estimate.
fieldHint.totalHours: Sum of hours from active time entries for this task. Voided or replaced source entries remain visible for audit but are excluded from this total.
fieldHint.firstActivity: Earliest work date among active time entries for this task. It is calculated from Work date—not entry creation time or planned Start—and changes when an entry is added, voided, or corrected.
fieldHint.lastActivity: Latest work date among active time entries for this task. It is calculated from Work date—not entry creation time or planned Finish—and excludes voided entries.
fieldHint.correctTime: Preserves the audit trail by voiding the original row and creating a new active replacement with the corrected values. This is not an in-place edit.
fieldHint.voidTime: Marks this entire record void without deleting it. Its hours immediately stop contributing to totals, actual dates, workload comparisons, and reports.
fieldHint.showVoided: Adds voided and replaced source rows to the audit table. Their values remain visible for review but never contribute to actual-hour totals or actual schedule windows.
fieldHint.comment: A Markdown task discussion entry. The comment is stored in the current draft, supports person mentions, and becomes durable history only after the draft changes are committed.
fieldHint.availabilityKind: Classifies an availability exception, such as vacation, sick leave, or another configured absence kind. It explains reduced capacity in calendars and workload views.
fieldHint.availabilityStart: First date affected by this availability exception. The range is inclusive and is applied together with Finish against the person's working calendar.
fieldHint.availabilityFinish: Last date affected by this availability exception. It is inclusive and cannot be earlier than Start.
fieldHint.availabilityPercent: Percentage of normal capacity that remains available during the date range: 100 means no reduction, 0 means unavailable, and intermediate values reduce daily capacity proportionally.
fieldHint.availabilityNote: Optional explanation for the availability exception. It provides context to planners but does not alter the percentage or date calculation.
fieldHint.availabilityState: Controls whether this availability record participates in calculations. Voided records remain in history but no longer reduce the person's capacity.
fieldHint.personEmail: Optional contact email used for display and assignee search. It is not a GitPM login, Git author identity, or permission grant.
fieldHint.personCapacity: The person's normal weekly capacity in hours, entered in quarter-hour increments. Scheduling distributes it over working days and then applies calendar and availability reductions.
fieldHint.personCalendar: The person's explicit working calendar: weekdays and holidays used with weekly capacity. The repository default is only the initial choice for a new person; saved people keep a reference to one specific calendar.
fieldHint.teamMembers: Active people included in this team. Team membership powers directory and workload filters; it does not assign members to projects or tasks automatically.
fieldHint.calendarPreset: Fills a new calendar with a predefined working week and holiday list. You can edit the generated name, weekdays, and dates before saving.
fieldHint.calendarWeekdays: Days of the week considered normally available for work. Capacity is distributed only across selected weekdays, except dates explicitly marked as holidays.
fieldHint.calendarHolidays: Specific non-working calendar dates. Holidays remove capacity even when their weekday is normally working; enter each date once in ISO calendar form.
fieldHint.defaultCalendar: Repository-wide fallback calendar. New people start with it, and people configured to inherit the default follow later changes; the current default cannot be archived.
fieldHint.configColor: Presentation color for this status or task type in badges and views. It is a fixed safe palette token and has no effect on validation or workflow semantics.
fieldHint.configActive: Active values are offered for new selections. Turning a value off preserves its technical ID and historical references, which is safer than deletion when old entities still use it.
fieldHint.visibleTaskFields: Chooses which task columns are visible in this plan view. It is a browser display preference only and does not clear assignees, dates, estimates, or statuses from tasks.
fieldHint.portfolioTaskColumns: Chooses which columns are visible in the all-tasks table. This is a browser display preference only and does not change stored tasks.
fieldHint.statusCategory: Semantic lifecycle category behind a custom status: backlog, active, done, or cancelled. Progress and completion logic use this category rather than guessing from the status name.
fieldHint.configSlug: Stable technical ID for a new status, task type, or work category. Use lowercase letters, digits, and internal hyphens; after creation it is intentionally not renamed because entities reference it.
fieldHint.trackKind: Manual tracks store entered dates, effort, and dependencies. The single actual track is computed from active time entries and cannot be edited as a manual schedule.
fieldHint.trackCapabilities: Declares which fields a manual track may store: dates, effort, and dependencies. Removing a capability that existing data or project planning relies on is rejected by repository validation.
fieldHint.trackSlug: Stable technical ID for a schedule track. Use lowercase letters, digits, and internal hyphens; tasks and project planning refer to this value, so it is not a display name.
fieldHint.boardProject: Chooses the project whose active tasks and configured statuses appear on the board. Dragging or changing a card status updates that task in the current draft.
fieldHint.boardStatus: Temporarily limits the board to one status. This is a view filter only and does not change any task.
fieldHint.boardType: Temporarily limits the board to one configured task type. This is a view filter only and does not change task classification.
fieldHint.savedView: Loads a saved project-scoped combination of board filters. Selecting or editing a view changes display settings; it does not copy or move tasks.
fieldHint.savedViewName: Human-readable name for a new saved board view. Saving creates a separate view from the current filters rather than overwriting another view.
fieldHint.ganttProject: Chooses the project rendered on the read-only Gantt chart. The chart reads schedule data; it does not reschedule tasks by dragging.
fieldHint.ganttScale: Changes horizontal zoom only: month, week, or day. It does not round, move, or rewrite any stored schedule date.
fieldHint.ganttPrimaryTrack: The date track drawn as the main bar for each row. Changing it only changes this chart's perspective and does not change the project's configured primary track.
fieldHint.ganttAdditionalTracks: Optional date tracks overlaid for visual comparison with the selected primary track. They remain read-only and do not affect workload calculations.
fieldHint.ganttDependencyTrack: The dependency-capable track whose predecessor links are drawn on the chart. It can differ from the date track used for bars.
fieldHint.workloadProject: Limits workload rows and task allocations to one project. Leave empty to aggregate all projects visible in the current draft.
fieldHint.workloadMilestone: Limits workload to tasks in one milestone, after the optional project filter. Changing this view filter does not move tasks between milestones.
fieldHint.workloadTeam: Limits workload rows to members of one team. Team membership filters people; it does not change task assignments or planned effort.
fieldHint.workloadPeriod: Shows the first 4, 8, 12, or all weeks of the calculated horizon, starting at the earliest week of matching tasks—not necessarily the current week. This view setting does not modify schedules.
fieldHint.actualMilestone: Limits actual-effort records to tasks in one milestone. The outside-active-milestones option includes tasks with no milestone and tasks referencing an unknown or archived milestone.
fieldHint.actualTask: Limits the report to one task. When Scope includes subtasks, entries from every descendant are included without double-counting the selected parent.
fieldHint.actualPerson: Limits actual records to work attributed to one person. It does not change task assignees and does not narrow the planned estimate shown beside the actual result.
fieldHint.actualCategory: Limits actual records to one configured work category. It does not filter tasks by task type and does not narrow the planned estimate.
fieldHint.actualFrom: Inclusive lower bound for the work date. It filters performed-on dates, not entry creation or Git commit timestamps.
fieldHint.actualTo: Inclusive upper bound for the work date. It filters performed-on dates, not entry creation or Git commit timestamps.
fieldHint.actualAfter: Cutoff used for the report's hours-after comparison. Only active entries with a work date strictly later than this date are summed.
fieldHint.actualScope: Task only counts the selected task's entries. With subtasks also includes all descendants in the task hierarchy while keeping unrelated tasks outside the result.
fieldHint.filterCombinator: AND requires every condition in this group to match. OR requires at least one; nested groups let you combine both without changing repository data.
fieldHint.sortField: Chooses the value used to compare rows. Sort rules have priority from top to bottom; each later rule breaks ties from earlier rules, and empty values always remain last.
fieldHint.sortDirection: Ascending means smaller numbers, earlier dates, and A–Z; descending reverses that order. Text comparison ignores case and recognizes numeric fragments.
fieldHint.filterField: Chooses the value to test. Changing the field resets the operator and entered value because each field has its own value type and supported comparisons.
fieldHint.filterOperator: Chooses how the field is compared. Text checks ignore case, Between includes both endpoints, Includes checks an exact list member, and Empty also covers missing values, empty strings, and empty lists.
fieldHint.filterValue: Value to compare using the selected field's type. Empty/not-empty and yes/no operators need no value; dates use calendar dates and option fields must use one of their configured values.
fieldHint.filterValueTo: Inclusive upper endpoint for a Between condition. Keep it later than or equal to the first date, or greater than or equal to the first number.
fieldHint.globalSearch: Searches the current working copy by entity ID or name across projects, tasks, milestones, people, teams, and calendars. Archived entities are included; descriptions and statuses are not searched. Use Ctrl/Cmd+K to focus.
fieldHint.commitMessage: One non-empty line up to 500 characters for the new Git commit. It records every current business change after full repository validation; committing does not push or merge the branch.
fieldHint.mergeRequestTitle: Required 1–255 character title of the GitLab Merge Request for the pushed draft branch. It is usually prefilled from the commit message but remains separate GitLab metadata.
fieldHint.mergeRequestDescription: Optional GitLab Merge Request details for reviewers. This text is sent to GitLab and is not stored as portfolio YAML.
fieldHint.commitId: Full 40–64 character hexadecimal Git object ID to inspect directly. The commit must exist in the repository; entering it does not change the working copy.
fieldHint.historySearch: Filters only the 50 loaded recent commits by subject, displayed author name, or SHA. It does not query all history or search commit bodies and files.
fieldHint.historyAuthor: Shows commits by one author from the loaded history. This filters display only and does not change permissions or authorship.
fieldHint.historyProject: Shows commits whose semantic change set contains paths below `projects/PROJECT-ID/…`. Values are technical project IDs; global configuration changes may not belong to any project.
fieldHint.historyDate: Shows commits from the selected calendar date according to recorded commit timestamps. It is unrelated to task due dates or time-entry work dates.
fieldHint.historyFiles: Filters the selected commit's changed-file list by path. It does not search file contents or alter the snapshot.
fieldHint.directRevertMessage: Commit message for the compensating commit created in direct mode. GitPM restores the selected historical state as a new change; existing history is not rewritten.
fieldHint.revertDraft: ID for a new draft that will contain the historical snapshot as reviewable changes. The current draft and existing commits remain unchanged.
fieldHint.exportFormat: Chooses a read-only representation: PDF report, static HTML site, UTF-8 CSV tables, spreadsheet workbook, or repository ZIP. Export never commits or publishes portfolio changes.
fieldHint.exportSections: Selects which report sections are generated. Unchecked sections are omitted from this file only; portfolio data is not deleted.
fieldHint.exportProjects: Adds an overview of active projects with status, owner, active task and milestone counts, finish date, and calculated schedule risk.
fieldHint.exportPeople: Adds an overview of active people with their projects, teams, weekly capacity, and working calendar. Archived people are omitted from this section.
fieldHint.exportProjectDetails: Adds a detailed page for every active project with active milestones, operational tasks, assignees, planned schedule, and actual effort.
fieldHint.exportGantt: Adds a Gantt page for every active project using operational tasks and the current schedule-track configuration.
fieldHint.exportPlanFact: Adds plan versus actual hours by task, person, category and date using the project's workload track.
fieldHint.exportWorkload: Adds weekly allocated hours, capacity and overload from the shared workload formula.
fieldHint.exportVacations: Adds absences, overlap and annual leave balances from the shared vacation calculations.
fieldHint.exportPersonProfile: Adds a profile for each selected person with projects, assigned tasks, absences and leave balance.
fieldHint.exportAudit: Adds archived entities, voided time entries, comments and recent commit history.
fieldHint.exportLifecycle: Chooses whether the report includes active entities, archived entities, or both.
fieldHint.exportEmail: When checked, rendered reports may include person email addresses. Email stays hidden by default.
fieldHint.exportGit: Repository ZIP only: includes portable `.git` history while removing origin URLs and reflogs. A linked worktree becomes a standalone Git copy, so the archive can be much larger.
fieldHint.repositoryUrl: Git remote used to fetch and push the active branch. Use an HTTP(S) or SSH repository address without embedding usernames, passwords, or access tokens.
fieldHint.gitlabUrl: Base URL of the GitLab instance used for OAuth, membership checks, and Merge Requests. Do not include a project path here.
fieldHint.gitlabProject: GitLab namespace and project path, for example group/project. It must identify the same repository as the configured Git origin.
fieldHint.gitlabClientId: Public OAuth application identifier registered for GitPM. It is not a client secret; GitLab integration requires this value together with the base URL and project path.
fieldHint.fileName: New file or folder name inside the draft worktree. Path separators, traversal segments, reserved guidance paths, and names outside the allowed workspace boundary are rejected.
fieldHint.peopleTaskStatus: Shows this person's tasks whose current status is checked. The filter changes only the profile list; it does not update task status.
fieldHint.peopleTaskProject: Shows this person's tasks from the checked projects. The filter changes only the profile list and does not move or reassign tasks.
